# Service Menu Build for The Forge

**Get it done fast — here's the real work:**

• **Start with your ACTUAL revenue** — pull last 3 months of transactions, group by service type (group classes, PT, packages, add-ons). This shows what's *actually* selling, not what you think should sell. Build your menu around proven money-makers first.

• **Create two separate docs immediately** — one "member-facing" (clean, benefits-focused, pricing clear), one "coach operations sheet" (what's included in each offering, what upsells exist, commission/compensation structure). Coaches need to know where the $ comes from to sell it.

• **Price anchor to your best seller** — identify your highest-margin or most-booked offering, then position everything else relative to it. If PT is your star, price packages as multiples of single sessions. Removes decision paralysis.

• **Add one "VIP/premium tier" immediately** — even if it's just priority booking + nutrition check-ins. High-ticket offerings don't need volume; they justify their own margin and create urgency around standard tiers.

• **Lock it down and communicate ruthlessly** — once finalized, send to coaches with *one* required meeting to walk through it (15 mins max). Inconsistent messaging kills conversion. Then post it publicly and start using it in every sales conversation this week.

**Insights**

- July was an anomaly driven by volume—215 leads at £2/lead looks like either a technical tracking issue, audience overlap, or a creative that saturated fast. August corrected to 109 leads at £5/lead, which is actually *healthy* and sustainable. Your close rate (22%) is solid; the issue isn't lead quality, it's consistency.
- You've cracked the conversion funnel (22% close is strong for a gym trial), but your cost-per-lead is creeping back up month-on-month (£6 → £14 → £21 → £2 → £5). This suggests creative fatigue and audience exhaustion—you're hitting the same cold audiences repeatedly without refresh.
- August's £52 profit per trial sold is workable, but it's margins-thin. You need either lower CAC or higher close rate to scale confidently.

**Actions**

1. **Pause and segment your July audience.** That 215-lead month tells you there's a winning creative or audience in there. Pull the top 3 performing ad variants from July and test them fresh against a *new* cold audience in September (lookalike off your 29 July converters, or interest-stack women 25–45 into wellness/fitness you haven't hit in 60+ days). Isolate what actually worked.

2. **Test 3 new creative angles immediately.** You're suffering creative decay. Run: (a) user-generated testimonial from your 24 August converters (social proof), (b) pain-point reframe (busy working mum / post-baby / stress relief—not just "fitness"), (c) urgency/scarcity (6-week trial, limited spots). Keep spend equal across all three; kill the losers by day 7.

3. **Tighten your audience to high-intent only.** Stop broad cold targeting. Use a LAL (lookalike) audience built from your 24 August paying customers only, and layer in: women 28–42, Belfast/surrounding 5 miles, interests in weight loss + mental health + women's spaces (not just fitness). Shrink your audience size to force relevance; you'll pay more per impression

# THE FORGE — FRACTIONAL CFO BRIEF

## REVENUE — CRITICAL ACTIONS

• **Arrest the rev/member collapse.** Aug at £97/member is 32% down from Jul's £142 and way below your Jan–Jul average of £129. You've added 27 members since May (111→166) but revenue per head has tanked. Immediate audit: are new members on discounted rates? Are existing members downgrading tiers? You're leaving £900–£1,200/month on the table. Enforce price consistency and fast-track new joiners onto standard rate after month 1.

• **Churn spike in May (12.8%) was a one-off (now back to 3–8% range).** Good. But your Aug *net* member growth masks soft underlying retention — you're recruiting hard to offset leakage. Focus Q4 on *keeping* the 166 you have, not just adding. Run a win-back campaign on lapsed members from May; offer 3-month loyalty discounts only to existing base.

• **Class occupancy and peak-hour pricing.** You don't have class data, but with 166 active members you should be hitting near-capacity in peak slots (6–8 a.m., 5–7 p.m.). Introduce surge pricing (£3–5 premium for peak classes booked within 48 hours) and off-peak incentives (free class or £2 discount 10–11 a.m., 2–4 p.m.). Target: shift 8–10 members/month to quiet slots = £96–120 extra revenue at zero cost.

• **New revenue line: personal training / small-group coaching.** At £97/member, standalone membership margin is thin. Offer 1-to-1 PT at £40–50/session (typical Belfast rate) to your top 20 engaged members; aim for 2–3 takers at 2 sessions/month = £160–300 extra. Alternatively, "6-week shred" bootcamp packages at £120/person to non-members. You have a bigger studio now (post-relocation); use the space.

---

## EXPENSES — WHERE TO TIGHTEN

• **August cash burn is unsustainable.** Net cash was –£5,335 (revenue £16,160, outgoings £28,693). Excluding the planned April relocation shock, your last 3 months average –£1,408 net cash *despite* growing membership. This means fixed costs (rent, utilities, insurance, payroll) are too high relative to current revenue.
